ket-bra-bridge: What range of numbers can be a probability? Check the size of the factor multiplying the state.
Track the factor once in the amplitude and again in its complex conjugate. What survives in their product?
state-coordinates: Which entry sits beside e₃? The largest coefficient belongs to a different label.
You have read the size of the coefficient. What step turns that size into an outcome probability?
outer-product-action: A projector keeps the part already pointing its way. How much of the minus direction lies along plus?
Compare the input with the direction the filter keeps. Would the whole input pass that filter?
unitary-basis-change: Which coordinates describe the new state? Be sure the state and the matrix use the same basis.
Look at the occupied entry of the old state. Is the first or second original direction selected?
adjoints-and-observables: Compare the entry above the diagonal with the complex conjugate of the entry below it.
After swapping rows and columns, each diagonal value returns to its own place. Must those two values match each other?
spectral-projectors: The preparation has changed. Read the new coefficient on the state with the requested energy.
Match 4E₀ to its energy direction first. Which coefficient belongs to that direction?
degeneracy-and-compatible-set: Apply A before and after swapping e₁ and e₂. Does A give those two directions different energy labels?
Imagine measuring A on either of the two swapped directions. Could the swap remain hidden from that measurement?
operator-functions: Write the second phase angle with the new θ before locating it on a circle.
Check whether the second phase arrow has made a full turn at this θ.
projector-probability: Mark every entry that survives the projector. Have you counted the squared size of each one?
What happens to the nonzero third entry when you apply a projector with a zero there?
degenerate-luders: After the energy filter, keep the signs of the two surviving components. How do they combine in the plus direction?
Compare the surviving state’s relative sign with the sign required for the plus direction.
sequential-filters: Which part of the ensemble reaches the first filter’s output? It still has another filter to pass.
This number describes passing one step. How many particles got as far as that step?
complete-projective-measurement: Think about two perpendicular directions on a rotated grid. Can they still cover the same whole plane?
The minus sign belongs to an amplitude. What happens when you take its squared size?
commutator-products: Write the two matrix products in order and simplify the adjacent pair of Zs. Which matrix remains?
Does X switch the sign picked out by Z? Try each product on the same starting column.
covariance-uncertainty: List the possible Z readings for this specific state. How far is each allowed reading from their mean?
A difference between two possible Z labels is not yet a variance. Which labels actually occur here?
translation-generator: The displacement is signed. On a number line, which way should you move from +1 when a is negative?
Start at the marked initial centre, rather than at zero, and count the signed steps.
parity-operator: Does putting i beside one component change its probability weight? Compare the weights of the two parities.
An average parity uses both possible signs. Is the state made only of its even part?
spectral-time-evolution: Sketch the two contributions to the plus output as arrows. After the phase change, do the arrows still point together?
A sure plus result would mean the state still matches the starting plus state. Did both energy components gain the same phase?
heisenberg-picture: Draw 2π/3 on a circle. Which side of the vertical axis contains the tip?
Both descriptions use the same preparation and measurement. What did one description move from the state to the operator?
ordered-time-steps: Write the two phase factors for one diagonal entry. Does swapping multiplication order require equal durations?
Try multiplying two diagonal matrices entry by entry in reverse order. What could change?
conserved-observables: Look for the t printed directly in A(t). Does the commutator account for that dependence?
What factor does the identity operation give on every normalized state?
spin-preparation: Read the coefficient beside +z before taking its squared size. Does that component have the whole state’s weight?
The second component includes i. Can it cancel the first component when the detector reads +z?
pauli-matrices: Apply the two diagonal entries of Z separately. Which input component is multiplied by a minus sign?
Does Z reverse every component, or does it act differently on the two entries?
spin-direction-eigenstates: For θ less than a right angle, the +n direction is closer to +z than −n is. Did you choose the matching projection?
Equal chances arise for a perpendicular measurement. What is the angle in this question?
bloch-pure-state: Which outcome does the positive y projection favour? The question asks for the opposite sign.
A zero probability would require exact alignment with +y. Check the length of the y component on its own.
spinor-rotation: Picture the +x arrow after a half-turn about z. What angle now separates it from the +x detector?
A full turn would bring a direction back to its start. How much of a turn does π describe?
magnetic-precession: Track the sign of the rotation angle in the time-evolution rule when γ changes sign.
A turn around the field keeps the spin’s component along that field fixed. Where did the spin start?
two-level-hamiltonian: Write the two levels as a common centre plus and minus the splitting term. What cancels when subtracting?
A single shifted level is not the distance between the levels. Find both endpoints first.
coupled-state-oscillations: Calculate the angle Ωt/2, then ask for the sine squared at that particular time.
The transfer can peak before the time asked about. How much of the oscillation has elapsed?
detuning-and-avoided-crossing: Look at where the sign of Δ enters the squared frequency. Could a probability ever become negative?
A detuned drive need not transfer the entire population. Check the factor in front of the oscillating term.
rotating-frame-bridge: If two clocks rotate together, is the rate seen by one clock the sum or the difference?
Measure the drive relative to the natural rotation. What would a co-rotating observer see when their rates match?
rabi-approximation: This question asks for one instant, not the average over a cycle. Find the accumulated half-angle.
Check the time of the first full transfer and compare it with the specified time.
coherent-number-expansion: The probability uses the size of α. Where would a minus sign come from after taking its size squared?
Imagine the tip of α turning from 1 to i on a circle. How far is it from zero afterward?
displacement-operator: Check the order of D and its adjoint on the two sides of a. Which order is used by the stated shift rule?
This operation shifts an amplitude. Does the rule use α itself or its squared size?
coherent-quadratures: Moving the centre of a wave packet is different from squeezing its width. Which change does this α describe?
Which part of α controls the centre reading? Which quantities set the width of a coherent state?
coherent-evolution: Draw the real-axis arrow for α₀, then turn it through π. Which way does its real part point?
When would that rotating arrow point entirely along the imaginary axis? Check the angle.
coherent-number-comparison: Which preparation fixes the particle count exactly, the number state or the coherent state?
Compare the variance rule for a coherent state with the rule for its mean squared.
tensor-basis: Pair each choice for A with every choice for B. Would adding the two counts list all possible pairs?
Start by listing the pairs for just one of A’s states. What about its other two states?
local-operator-tensor: Read the two symbols in X⊗I from left to right. Which one acts on B, the second digit?
This is an operation on a joint state. What kind of result would taking an overlap produce instead?
joint-measurements: Is any outcome on A being kept or discarded? Check whether the question asks for a conditional chance.
List all pairs whose B entry is 1. Have you included each possible A entry?
composite-hamiltonian: The interaction changes relative phases over time. Does it also remove three of the four basis amplitudes?
Time evolution here preserves the total probability. Could the proposed result still be normalized?
density-from-preparations: If the source sends a plus state, does a 0/1 detector always read 0?
Count detections from both ways the source prepares the system. Can the plus preparation contribute any zeros?
trace-expectation: Look at the weights for the two opposite readings of Z. Would their contributions cancel exactly?
This is a mean, not a single positive reading. How should the negative readings enter?
density-positivity: Draw a vector with these x and y components. Does validity depend on its length or on the number of nonzero entries?
Equal eigenvalues correspond to the centre of the Bloch ball. How far is the given point from that centre?
partial-trace: A plus-direction measurement uses both coordinate directions together. Have you included the entries off the diagonal?
Test the opposite, minus direction too. Would this reduced state assign it no weight at all?
purity-and-unrecorded-measurement: Which two weights are you squaring? Are the stated 0/1 outcomes equally likely?
Were you told which result happened? Distinguish a selected result from a measurement whose result was forgotten.
product-or-entangled: Try to factor the two-by-two coefficient table. What must its determinant be if it comes from one product?
Normalization checks total probability. What separate test checks whether the pair can be split into two states?
schmidt-decomposition: Count the Schmidt weights that are actually nonzero, not the number of spaces on the list.
Would a state still have weight anywhere if one entry is exactly one?
two-spin-correlations: Certain agreement would require perfect positive correlation. What correlation goes with perpendicular axes here?
Which angle gives certain opposite results in a singlet? Compare that angle with a right angle.
bell-chsh-bound: Write all four terms with their signs before taking the absolute value. What sign belongs in front of the last correlation?
Check whether the final positive correlation is added or subtracted before looking for cancellation.
local-no-signalling: Did A learn which outcome B obtained? Which outcomes must still be included from A’s point of view?
Use this preparation’s local weights rather than the balanced weights of the earlier example.
angular-ladder-spectrum: In the raising formula, write both j(j+1) and m(m+1) under the square root before subtracting.
The highest allowed m tells you where raising stops. Does it alone give the factor on this rung?
spin-one-matrices: A negative sign belongs to the central amplitude. What happens to that sign when finding a chance?
In the displayed order, which of the three entries labels the zero z-component?
orbital-rotation-action: Check whether you selected the original x direction or the perpendicular direction after rotation.
Did you compute the projection amplitude or the probability made from it?
angular-rotation-matrices: Rotating a spin-one state distributes its weight among three possible z readings. Check the coefficient for the middle one.
Find the sine of this angle before squaring the middle entry. Where does its normalization factor enter?
angular-expectation-spread: Knowing one component exactly does not settle the other directions. Which direction did the prepared spin rotate into?
Start with the sharp axis before rotation. Where does a quarter-turn take it?
total-angular-operators: Start at the smallest allowed total value and count up in whole steps. Does your proposed value appear?
Compare the proposal with the sum of the two individual angular-momentum labels.
singlet-triplet: The squared total angular momentum uses j(j+1). What j labels the triplet?
The label M gives one component. Does a zero component mean the whole angular momentum is zero?
unequal-angular-addition: Look at the coefficient of the smaller total-j sector. Did you use the weight of the other sector?
Is the square root a state coefficient or a measurement probability?
coupled-basis-measurements: Passing the first measurement gets you only partway through the sequence. What fraction of those outcomes pass the next selection?
After keeping j=1/2, read the m₁=0 weight of that state, then account for how often it was prepared.
spin-orbit-energy: The upper level’s shift is only one end of the gap. Where is the other end?
Use each sector’s angular-momentum factor with λ before comparing the levels.
exchange-postulate: An electron’s state includes more than its location. Which other label travels with it when the electrons are exchanged?
The two particle slots are labels in a calculation. Can different slot numbers change what properties belong to an electron?
symmetric-pair-normalization: Compute how much of v lies along u. Does the cross term vanish for these two choices?
Check whether every component of v matches u. What overlap would identical states need?
fermion-determinant: Pauli exclusion concerns two identical full states. Are these plus and minus combinations actually the same state?
Does “one in each mode” distinguish which particle was written first? Count all ordered ways it can happen.
spin-spatial-symmetry: Multiply the sign from the spatial part by the proposed spin sign. Does the product have the required fermion sign?
The rule applies after combining space and spin. What sign should the complete state acquire?
occupation-and-filling: Try filling the lowest mode with both fermions. How many are allowed in one full spinless mode?
Order the three modes by energy. Must either particle skip an available lower mode?
exchange-energy: Write the one-body sum in both energy expressions. What happens to shared terms when you subtract?
Does the direct interaction have opposite signs in the two expressions, or the same sign?
spin-sequence-capstone: This number may describe getting through the +z filter. What still has to happen at the −x filter?
Only spins that passed the first filter reach the second one. What fraction of the original group was that?
two-level-capstone: The maximum possible transfer is not the transfer at every time. Evaluate the oscillating part at the stated angle.
Check both the size of the allowed oscillation and its phase at this particular moment.
composite-exchange-capstone: After B’s selected result, is A described by two independent chances or by two amplitudes with a relative sign?
Write the new minus sign before taking the overlap with +y. Does the imaginary part help the other term or oppose it?
quantum2-assessment: Try multiplying this real table by the column (1, −1). Does the result point along that column or turn it around?
Two numbers can add to one in many ways. Check each eigenvalue, the number by which the table scales a matching direction.
